\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সংঘর্ষ} (sôngghôrshô)}{সংঘর্ষ (sôngghôrshô)}]{\bn{সংঘর্ষ} (sôngghôrshô) — a collision; a clash}

\label{lesson:BN-C391-songghorsho}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for tar, then the Bengali for to roll.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সংঘর্ষ}}
\textbf{\bn{সংঘর্ষ}} — \emph{sôngghôrshô} — \textquotedblleft{}a collision; a clash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{মোড়ে} \bn{একটা} \bn{বাস} \bn{আর} \bn{একটা} \bn{ট্রাকের} \bn{সংঘর্ষ} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{moṛe ekṭā bās ār ekṭā ṭrāker sôngghôrshô hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A bus and a lorry collided at the crossroads.
\end{quote}

A word of the news: the paper reports a \bn{সংঘর্ষ} where a witness says the two vehicles hit each other.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সংঘর্ষ}} (\emph{sôngghôrshô}) is Sanskrit \emph{saṃgharṣa}, \textquotedblleft{}rubbing together, friction, rivalry\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams); the sense of two vehicles meeting is the modern use.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôngghôrshô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôngghôrshô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{moṛe ekṭā bās ār ekṭā ṭrāker sôngghôrshô hôlô.} — A bus and a lorry collided at the crossroads.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for tar, then the Bengali for to roll, then say \emph{sôngghôrshô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সংঘর্ষ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A collision; a clash\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{টলা} (ṭôlā)}{টলা (ṭôlā)}]{\bn{টলা} (ṭôlā) — to totter; to sway}

\label{lesson:BN-C391-tola}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to roll, then the Bengali for a collision.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{টলা}}
\textbf{\bn{টলা}} — \emph{ṭôlā} — \textquotedblleft{}to totter; to sway\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ভিড়ের} \bn{ধাক্কায়} \bn{বুড়ো} \bn{লোকটা} \bn{টলে} \bn{উঠল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhiṛer dhākkāy buṛo lokṭā ṭôle uṭhlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Jostled by the crowd, the old man tottered.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{টললেন}, \emph{tini ṭôllen}.

Not \bn{তোলা}, to lift: \bn{ট} and \bn{ত} are different letters.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{টলা}} (\emph{ṭôlā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{ṭalan}, \textquotedblleft{}staggering, slipping\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{ṭálati}, \textquotedblleft{}moves aside, is disturbed\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5450).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭôlā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭôlā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhiṛer dhākkāy buṛo lokṭā ṭôle uṭhlô.} — Jostled by the crowd, the old man tottered.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to roll, then the Bengali for a collision, then say \emph{ṭôlā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{টলা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To totter; to sway\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নড়া} (nôṛā)}{নড়া (nôṛā)}]{\bn{নড়া} (nôṛā) — to budge; to stir}

\label{lesson:BN-C391-nora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a collision, then the Bengali for to totter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নড়া}}
\textbf{\bn{নড়া}} — \emph{nôṛā} — \textquotedblleft{}to budge; to stir\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{যানজটে} \bn{বাসটা} \bn{এক} \bn{ঘণ্টা} \bn{নড়ল} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jānjôṭe bāsṭā ek ghônṭā nôṛlô nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the traffic jam the bus did not budge for an hour.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{গাড়ি} \bn{নড়ল}, \emph{sei gāṛi nôṛlô}.

\bn{নাড়ানো}, to stir or to wave, is the causing partner.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নড়া}} (\emph{nôṛā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{naṛā}, \textquotedblleft{}to shake, to flinch, to move\textquotedblright{}, under the reconstructed \emph{naṭati} (CDIAL 6934).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôṛā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôṛā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jānjôṭe bāsṭā ek ghônṭā nôṛlô nā.} — In the traffic jam the bus did not budge for an hour.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a collision, then the Bengali for to totter, then say \emph{nôṛā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ছাড়ানো} (chhāṛāno)}{ছাড়ানো (chhāṛāno)}]{\bn{ছাড়ানো} (chhāṛāno) — to overtake; to get past; to peel}

\label{lesson:BN-C391-chharano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to totter, then the Bengali for to budge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ছাড়ানো}}
\textbf{\bn{ছাড়ানো}} — \emph{chhāṛāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to overtake; to get past; to peel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাসটা} \bn{একটা} \bn{ট্রাককে} \bn{ছাড়িয়ে} \bn{গেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāsṭā ekṭā ṭrākke chhāṛiye gelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bus overtook a lorry.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{বাস} \bn{ট্রাকটাকে} \bn{ছাড়াল}, \emph{sei bās ṭrākṭāke chhāṛālô}.

Mostly in the -\bn{এ} form with \bn{যাওয়া}: \bn{ছাড়িয়ে} \bn{যাওয়া}, to go past. Also to peel: \bn{কমলা} \bn{ছাড়ানো}, to peel an orange.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ছাড়ানো}} (\emph{chhāṛāno}) is the causing form of \textbf{\bn{ছাড়া}}, \textquotedblleft{}to leave, to let go\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{chardayati} (CDIAL 4998): to leave a vehicle behind, or a peel.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhāṛāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhāṛāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāsṭā ekṭā ṭrākke chhāṛiye gelô.} — The bus overtook a lorry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to totter, then the Bengali for to budge, then say \emph{chhāṛāno} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কষা} (kôshā)}{কষা (kôshā)}]{\bn{কষা} (kôshā) — to apply (the brakes); to tighten; to work out (a sum)}

\label{lesson:BN-C391-kosha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to budge, then the Bengali for to overtake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কষা}}
\textbf{\bn{কষা}} — \emph{kôshā} — \textquotedblleft{}to apply (the brakes); to tighten; to work out (a sum)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাস্তায়} \bn{গরু} \bn{দেখে} \bn{চালক} \bn{হঠাৎ} \bn{ব্রেক} \bn{কষলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāstāy gôru dekhe chālôk hôṭhāt brek kôshlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Seeing a cow on the road, the driver suddenly slammed on the brakes.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ব্রেক} \bn{কষলেন}, \emph{tini brek kôshlen}.

Also to pull a knot tight or to work out a sum on paper: a verb of pressing and rubbing hard.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কষা}} (\emph{kôshā}) probably goes back to Sanskrit \emph{kaṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}to rub, to scratch, to scrape\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): brakes, knots and sums are all worked by rubbing hard.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôshā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôshā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāstāy gôru dekhe chālôk hôṭhāt brek kôshlen.} — Seeing a cow on the road, the driver suddenly slammed on the brakes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to budge, then the Bengali for to overtake, then say \emph{kôshā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কষা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To apply (the brakes); to tighten; to work out (a sum)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Rails and Carriages to Collisions and Close Calls}

\label{lesson:BN-R391-review-384-391}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for a railway and a compartment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a railway, a compartment, a berth, a local train, to blow a whistle
  \item an hour, a clock, to tick (of a clock), to wait, a bench
  \item a porter, a suitcase, a trolley, to unload, to carry (a load)
  \item a path, a destination, a trip, to commute, return (of a journey)
  \item a tram, the metro, an autorickshaw, a van, to race
  \item a driver, a bus conductor, a helmet, to signal, to call out
  \item a highway, a bend, a pothole, tar, to roll
  \item a collision, to totter, to budge, to overtake, to apply (the brakes)
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A railway? (\textbf{\bn{রেল}}, \emph{rel}.) A compartment? (\textbf{\bn{কামরা}}, \emph{kāmrā}.) A berth? (\textbf{\bn{বার্থ}}, \emph{bārth}.) A local train? (\textbf{\bn{লোকাল}}, \emph{lokāl}.) To blow a whistle? (\textbf{\bn{হুইসল} \bn{দেওয়া}}, \emph{huisôl deoyā}.) An hour? (\textbf{\bn{ঘণ্টা}}, \emph{ghônṭā}.) A clock? (\textbf{\bn{ঘড়ি}}, \emph{ghôṛi}.) To tick (of a clock)? (\textbf{\bn{টিকটিক} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ṭikṭik kôrā}.) To wait? (\textbf{\bn{অপেক্ষা} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ôpekkhā kôrā}.) A bench? (\textbf{\bn{বেঞ্চ}}, \emph{bench}.) A porter? (\textbf{\bn{কুলি}}, \emph{kuli}.) A suitcase? (\textbf{\bn{সুটকেস}}, \emph{suṭkes}.) A trolley? (\textbf{\bn{ট্রলি}}, \emph{ṭrôli}.) To unload? (\textbf{\bn{নামানো}}, \emph{nāmāno}.) To carry (a load)? (\textbf{\bn{বহন} \bn{করা}}, \emph{bôhôn kôrā}.) A path? (\textbf{\bn{পথ}}, \emph{pôth}.) A destination? (\textbf{\bn{গন্তব্য}}, \emph{gôntôbyô}.) A trip? (\textbf{\bn{সফর}}, \emph{sôphôr}.) To commute? (\textbf{\bn{যাতায়াত} \bn{করা}}, \emph{jātāyāt kôrā}.) Return (of a journey)? (\textbf{\bn{ফিরতি}}, \emph{phirti}.) A tram? (\textbf{\bn{ট্রাম}}, \emph{ṭrām}.) The metro? (\textbf{\bn{মেট্রো}}, \emph{meṭro}.) An autorickshaw? (\textbf{\bn{অটো}}, \emph{ôṭo}.) A van? (\textbf{\bn{ভ্যান}}, \emph{bhæn}.) To race? (\textbf{\bn{দৌড়ানো}}, \emph{douṛāno}.) A driver? (\textbf{\bn{চালক}}, \emph{chālôk}.) A bus conductor? (\textbf{\bn{কন্ডাক্টর}}, \emph{kônḍākṭôr}.) A helmet? (\textbf{\bn{হেলমেট}}, \emph{helmeṭ}.) To signal? (\textbf{\bn{ইশারা} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ishārā kôrā}.) To call out? (\textbf{\bn{হাঁকা}}, \emph{hā̃kā}.) A highway? (\textbf{\bn{সড়ক}}, \emph{sôṛôk}.) A bend? (\textbf{\bn{বাঁক}}, \emph{bā̃k}.) A pothole? (\textbf{\bn{গর্ত}}, \emph{gôrtô}.) Tar? (\textbf{\bn{পিচ}}, \emph{pich}.) To roll? (\textbf{\bn{গড়ানো}}, \emph{gôṛāno}.) A collision? (\textbf{\bn{সংঘর্ষ}}, \emph{sôngghôrshô}.) To totter? (\textbf{\bn{টলা}}, \emph{ṭôlā}.) To budge? (\textbf{\bn{নড়া}}, \emph{nôṛā}.) To overtake? (\textbf{\bn{ছাড়ানো}}, \emph{chhāṛāno}.) To apply (the brakes)? (\textbf{\bn{কষা}}, \emph{kôshā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
